title: Sudanese group demand inquiry into shooting death
article: About 200 members of Calgary's Sudanese community left the funeral of a man fatally shot by police officers and marched to City Hall yesterday, calling for an independent judicial inquiry into his death.
Deng Kuol, 24, died Oct. 25 after a violent struggle with Const. Ira Macumber, who had been called to an apartment building to investigate a complaint about Kuol, who was reportedly drunk.
Police have said that Macumber, 40, was slashed in the arm with a knife and responded by firing two shots into Kuol's neck.

"The Sudanese community believes that there was no justification for the ultimate use of the deadly force," said Martin Yak, a spokesman for the Sudanese group. "We are asking for justice . . . we want the Alberta government to set up an independent inquiry."
Neither police Chief Jack Beaton nor Mayor Dave Bronconnier were available for comment.

Michael Shields of Alberta Justice said an independent fatality inquiry is mandatory in any case of a police shooting and will begin as soon as the Calgary Police Service completes its own investigation.
Friends of Kuol's have repeatedly questioned the chain of events that led to his death, saying Kuol wasn't a violent man.
However, he was wanted by RCMP in Brooks for breach of probation regarding a drunk-driving conviction.
Emotions ran high outside of city hall as friends lamented his death, particularly since he had escaped war-ravaged Sudan in the 1980s.
"Deng didn't need to run away from the war in Sudan to come and die in Canada," said an emotional Sidonia Amel, who grew up with Kuol in Bor, Sudan, and escaped to Cuba with him in the 1980s.
"If he has a gun and they shoot him, I understand. If he has a knife, I don't see a need to shoot him two times. If they shoot him once, he's helpless."
Kuol came to Canada in 1997 after spending 15 years in Cuba, where he fled after his mother and father were killed in his country's long-running civil war.
City police officials said they won't comment further until the investigation is complete.
